text_fidelity_a:
Mazama Intake Water Bladder | Easy to Fill and Leak Proof | Replacement for Hydration Reservoir for Backpacks and Day Packs I have other Mazama water bladders, and really wanted to like this. I bought it for a trip to the national parks in UT where you should be carrying more water. The good is that its a big reservoir, and the hose is thicker so the rate of flow is higher than their other hoses. What I love about Mazama is the magnetic holder for the hose, and this one is even better because there is some play in it where as the normal version can pop off at times (I generally wear it while mountain biking and its fine, but if there isn't enough slack in the hose it will pop off the magnet).

What I don't like about this one...the closure for the bladder is not secure. I found out by dumping about two liters of water over me when it was in my backpack and I bent forward. I know it looks like it should work, but because its plastic and malleable there is play there and its not perfect. The "lock" wiggles even without pressure, so its suspect to begin with. The way it opens is nice for cleaning, drying, and filling, and the "spine" is helpful for carrying and moving it around. These features cannot make up for the closure however, and I worry about it whenever the bladder is full. I'm also not a fan of the way the bite valve works...it can be left full open and water will just run out, or you can get it to work if you bite a little...but just a little because if you bit too much the rubber tip falls off. Squirely bugger.

When using in the future I might add a clamp or something to ensure the closure can't slip off, and will use my other hose vs this one.
text_fidelity_b: Mazama Intake Water Bladder | Easy to Fill and Leak Proof | Replacement for Hydration Reservoir for Backpacks and Day Packs

text_fidelity_a:
Stansport Aluminum Tent Peg, 9-Inch These stakes are well-constructed and can be pounded into reasonably hard soil without damage. I haven't destroyed any yet, but I do try to be careful when I'm pounding them into rocky ground. (A small, 8-ounce hammer works well. Larger hammers increase the likelihood of bending or breaking your stakes). The round cross section doesn't have the holding power of some of the flatter stake designs, so they don't hold as well in wind, in my experience. They're longer than most other after-market tent stakes, though (9 inches vs the more common 7-inches), which helps compensate. I like to have a few of these in my stake bag for places that the y-shaped stakes can't penetrate.

Some users have complained that they can't get their tent guylines through the holes in the silver heads. That isn't how they are intended to be used. Wrap your guyline or your anchor loop around the shaft of the stake, just below the silver head, and angle your stake to point it toward a point several feet below the center of your tent. These are fine stakes. Would like to try some of this style in a longer, 12-inch version, for larger tents that catch more wind and require stronger anchors.
text_fidelity_b: Stansport Aluminum Tent Peg, 9-Inch

text_fidelity_a:
Square36 NEW Exercise/Fitness Equipment Mat 12 Ft x 6 Ft. Highest Grade Materials. Our Fitness Mat Can Be Used For Cardio Workouts with or without shoes for fitness equipment We have been trying to up our game with exercise as Covid has gotten us out of the workout room and fully at home. When we added a heavy bag to make up for not being able to go back to our kickboxing guy we knew we needed something on the porch floor to protect our legs and feet. Based on existing reviews we knew we would be able to cut this if we needed to and that the thickness should be right. And with that hard cement we knew we wanted something to cushion us. So we chose this option.

It comes well wrapped in the included bag, strapped, and plastic. For our set up, the porch has a weird cut to it and we thought we’d have to cut the mat. Turns out we didn’t have to. The mat is thick enough to hold the heavy bag, but not so thick as to make it unsteady. We feel secure and we feel cushioned. Rolling it out we didn’t want the full amount, so we kept I partially rolled - so as to keep it away from the open end and any potential rain damage - and use the bag’s stand to hold the rest rolled in place. The width and length our perfect for this space and when we move we’ll have more or less depending - but not cutting it gives us options.

Working out on it has been fine. It gives security for footing - we do have one spot due to configuration, that makes it so we have to watch how far back we step, but it’s also not so high if we step funny we’ve had any issues. It gives good footing and we can punch full on - no worries. We are about to add a bench at the bottom end, that can be moved, so we’ll see how well that works, but based on the weight stand we’re confident it’ll be fine. We don’t know about marks it’ll leave - footprints from the weight of the stand or bench - but if we keep it in the same spot it’ll be fine.

Cleaning so far is easy - we have only had to wipe it down. We use our shoes on it and so far it’s been fine.

Overall we are really happy with this choice and think it’ll be a good mat for a long time, protecting us as we continue to workout.
text_fidelity_b: Square36 NEW Exercise/Fitness Equipment Mat 12 Ft x 6 Ft. Highest Grade Materials. Our Fitness Mat Can Be Used For Cardio Workouts with or without shoes for fitness equipment

I like that the filter is on the top of the bottle so no issues with stuff you are infusing leak out. I like the strap that is there to hold the bottle.

The not so good: The lid sometimes hits you in the face if you are not careful. It hit me already sometimes in the face. The area where you drink is right where the button of the flip lid is at and it pushes against your lower lip area when you drink. There is a hole on the top of the bottle which does LEAK if you try to drink it side wise. So you are forced to push your skin under your lip against the bottle lid button.

All in all, a good bottle but not perfect, still looking for that perfect bottle. I also did some research on plastic, as this is tritan but it is not plastic safe either. Wanted glass really but there are no infusion glass bottles. I also considered steel but then you can't see into the bottle. Someone needs to make a steel bottle with glass on the side or something. I guess the threshold for how much people will pay for the bottle limits the options of what is out there.

text_fidelity_a:
Base+ Standing Desk Balance Board Aluminum Bamboo Wobble Board Ergonomic Office Standing Desk Accessories Wooden Balancing Platform footrest Easy Gentle 360 Motion Silver I've had this board a few weeks now, and I really enjoy it. I use my standing desk so much more now because the motion this board allows is actually fun. The board is very sturdy and mostly stays in place pretty well.

I have two complaints:

1. The surface is hard, so my feet get sore after standing on it for more than 30-45 minutes. I just ordered a small anti-fatigue standing mat that I'll have to cut to fit this board - maybe that will help. But I wish this board came with the option of a correctly-sized cushioned mat. If my feet weren't in pain, I'd probably stand on this more than half time, if not full time.

2. The description says "Stand Still | gently rock, tip, twist | aggressively balance, move & surf". I bought this model specifically because it said "twist". But it doesn't twist. The bottom of the ball is grippy rubber with knobs that make it even grippier, especially on the thin commercial carpet typically found in offices. The grippy rubber knobs are good for keeping it in place, but they completely prevent the board from twisting. You can force it to twist a little bit if you need to move it 1/2" forward or back, but you can not absent-mindedly twist while you're working. Also, while technically you can tip / rock forward and back, really the only motion that's at all natural is rocking side to side. It's really good for rocking side to side. Any other motion requires enough effort to make it a distraction from working.

I'll keep this, because I really do enjoy the motion, and this is a very high quality board for this price point. But I'll probably also order a Fluidstance board because I really want the twisting motion, and I need a higher weight limit, so I'll end up ordering their top-of-the-line, which is ~4.5 times the price of this board. Alas. If only this board actually twisted....
text_fidelity_b: Base+ Standing Desk Balance Board Aluminum Bamboo Wobble Board Ergonomic Office Standing Desk Accessories Wooden Balancing Platform footrest Easy Gentle 360 Motion Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Black, Pedometer, Small/Large I've had my Fitbit Flex for about a week. At first, I was fairly impressed when I actually counted my steps and compared it to the Fitbit calculations. However, it can be very quirky and inaccurate under certain circumstances. I have mine on my right wrist, and I am right-handed, so I made sure to set it to the "Dominant" wrist setting. But, to get truly accurate readings, your arm really needs to be at your side. If I'm carrying things around the house, I don't get an accurate count. If I'm walking through the store, pushing a grocery cart, I don't get an accurate count. It seriously under counts my steps. I'd like to send it back and exchange it for the Fitbit One, which I have since heard is more accurate. However, I didn't realize that Amazon only takes returns on unopened items, and otherwise charges a restocking fee. And, I'm not sure this is defective. I think it's just not accurate. Should have bought this from a Brick & Mortar store.

Edited 4/1/2014...Ok, I've been using my Fitbit for a few more days. Today I was out for several hours and my step count was still really low as, described previously, I don't walk with my hands down at my side. I'm usually busy doing other things. I had contacted Fitbit regarding the problem, but the only thing they could say was that it compared to other wrist-trackers on the market....which isn't saying a lot. I'd really like to return or exchange this thing, but can't. When I got home this afternoon, and saw that my step count was again very low, I decided to try taking the Flex unit out of the wrist band and I put it in my pocket. So far, that seems to give me a better step count. Not sure how it will work that way with the other functions. But, frankly, after using the Flex for over a week, I'm not confident in the accuracy of the other functions and will probably never use them. There is an Omron brand clip-on that gets rave reviews. Check that one out before you decide to buy the Flex.

Edited 4/3/2014...I pursued my issues with Fitbit customer service, and this is what they said: " Flex will count your steps when you're walking with your arms stationary, as we do want to give you credit for this activity. This includes walking while pushing a stroller or shopping cart, or holding on to a treadmill. However, because your hands are not moving, your step count may be a bit lower during this activity."

So, they have finally admitted the count is not accurate unless your arms are down at your side. I do dispute the fact that it is a "bit lower." My steps are hardly being counted at all, unless my arm is down at my side. So, for this reason, I have now lowered my rating to two stars. I did contact Amazon customer service and explained what was going on. They are allowing me to return it, without restocking charges, because it is not working as intended. THANKS AMAZON!!!
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Black, Pedometer, Small/Large

text_fidelity_a:
Lumina 900 Boost Front Bike Light Sabre 80 Rear Bike Light Combo Pack, Black, 900 Lumens Front / 80 Lumens Rear Overall, I'm happy with my purchase as I feel I received good value for the money spent. Both lights operate as described and (mostly) provide me with the light I was seeking for my very early morning or very late night rides. I am a full-time bike commuter who lives and works in the suburbs and drivers here are notoriously distracted and inattentive.

Specifically, the front light has a great mount, better than I expected. Holds well to my odd-shapped handlebars. My rating of a C+ is based on two issues I have with the beam of the light. It seems to loose its stated 900 lumens brightness about 30-40 minutes into my ride. It's almost as though I can see it getting dim as I ride. Additionally, it shines a large circle of light rather than an oval-shaped beam that I grew used to on my Cygolite and Cycle Torch lights on my other bikes. I much prefer the oval beam for seeing a nice wide angle. As for the tail light, I'm very pleased. It offers great brightness by night and day, which here in the 'burbs is very important. My only knock on the tail light is that is must be charged after every use. The battery life is 60 minutes tops.

If you don't mind charging your lights after every use, even short rides, and a circular headlight beam meets your needs, I think you would be happy with this light set. I would absolutely purchase Nite Rider tail lights again, however because of the round beam and the dimming of the headlight after just a short while, I don't know that I would buy another head light from this company. Too bad because I think I like their mounting strap better than any other I've used.
text_fidelity_b: Lumina 900 Boost Front Bike Light Sabre 80 Rear Bike Light Combo Pack, Black, 900 Lumens Front / 80 Lumens Rear

text_fidelity_a:
Elimoons Silicone Wedding Ring for Men - 10 Rings&Singles Silicone Rubber Wedding Bands- 8.7 mm Wide - 2.5mm Thick I’ve had my eye on another brand for awhile, but wasn’t sure - a single ring is around $25 - being concerned the silicone wouldn’t work, feel good, or have any give. My ring finger tapers and can go up and down during the day, so metal rings can go from loose to tight. Would this kind work? While not metal pricing, I still didn’t want to pay for another ring to sit in the drawer.

I am thrilled with these rings.

First, I got two sets: I literally fell on the line between the two sizes so figured it would be smarter than risking it. My ring finger is the smaller of the two, but I still get use of the larger set on other fingers. Usually not at the same time - looks a little goofy.

Second, I wasn’t sure on the grip - would they work on my tapered finger and would they have any give. Yes to both. In fact the only time I have an “issue” with being loose is washing my hands. I have to watch a bit, holding fingers tight, but otherwise the rings both stay snug and on, as well as give a little when humidity expands them. I love the fit, the size and look on my finger, and that little give.

Third, Yes, I keep them on when washing my hands, but I do take the ring off to dry it as well. Otherwise it will retain moisture - it does get annoying and loosens the fit. I have worn them to shower, but now keep it off, just in case.

Forth, working out and doing things with them on is a breeze. I lift weights (with/without gloves) play pickle ball, do chores, you name it, and the rings hold up. There is no issue and I don’t have to worry about damaging, bending, or otherwise having any problems.

Fifth, The Colors... Interesting. Some I love and look really nice on their own and on my hand. Some I just don’t like. It’s a personal taste thing, but some look cartoonish or goofy. Overall, it’s a personal thing, so have some fun. I was surprised I liked the look of the bright blue, red (thought I’d hate it), and tie dye.

Sixth, there is a slight difference between the cuts of these two sets I got. I include image to show: one is rounded, the other sharp cut. Not sure you can tell from product page the difference - I didn’t until they arrived.

These are some great rings for the price and I do like that I got different sizes. I do wear the larger ones on other fingers from time to time, but I love that I can now wear a wedding ring and not worry. (* Same review given for the other set in order to stay consistent with my experience)
text_fidelity_b: Elimoons Silicone Wedding Ring for Men - 10 Rings&Singles Silicone Rubber Wedding Bands- 8.7 mm Wide - 2.5mm Thick

text_fidelity_a:
Moxi Skates - Beach Bunny - Fashionable Womens Roller Skates Color: Watermelon. Skate Size: 7 (My normal shoe/boot size is 8-8.5 in US womens)
First, they are soooo cute! I love the color combo. I'm 50 yrs old and decided to get back into roller skating. I used to do this casually when I was in my teens, but was never exceptional at it. I thought this would be a fun way to get some more exercise in my life. So far its working! You engage so many muscles when roller skating. It takes balance, core and leg strength to keep from falling on your bum. These are made of vinyl so they are quite stiff at first and take some time break in. My hubby purchased these as a gift. He purchased according to the size chart and they fit well/snug with a thick sock. I normally wear a size 8 in U.S women’s shoes. When it comes to boots I typically buy 8.5 (to allow for thicker sock). Hubby purchased the size 7 skates as the chart indicated. This was just right. I thought they might be a bit tight at first. But with use, I realized the size was perfect. You want your foot to be held firmly as you will be moving around a lot. I imagine if they were looser, my foot would flex more and potentially cause strain in the foot muscles so I think the snug sizing is perfect. Measure your foot and look at size chart and you should be fine. I like that the skates have a metal base plate instead of plastic. This feels sturdier/safer. The wheels roll well on blacktop streets (even better on my hardwood floors inside my house). There are a couple things that were a bit odd. First the vinyl is so thick its a bit uncomfortable (specifically around the ankle) until they get worn in. And it takes a while to wear them in.
Second, the laces on one skate were a whole foot longer than the laces on the other skate. This trips out my OCD brain. I will have to replace them.

Overall, I think these are good skates for beginners (of all ages). They are made well and of good quality. Just be patient with the wear in period.

Coleman Evanston Tent Updated Sept 2022. Purchased in 2018:

We use this tent three to five times per year depending on how many people are going. This is a great tent! The instructions on whether or not to use the black poles or the grey poles for the main tent could be clearer, but we wrote that on the bag after setting it up incorrectly twice.

I would not classify this as a three season tent, unless you live in a warmer climate. I live in central Texas, so this will work for me almost year round.

The good :
-very spacious, Large framed door on hinges.
-Good Head room.
-Lots of mesh on roof and two sides.
-Rain fly has excellent coverage over all openings but still allows adequate ventilation.
-Bath-tub floor comes up really high.
-Appears to be good reinforcement at stress points.

The bad :
- Really needs two people to set up (but I suppose if you are buying a tent this large you will have help).
- Stakes. As with any tent now a days, you probably won't be using the stakes that are included.

Buying experience - The tent arrived well before the stated delivery date, and the packaging was in excellent condition.

We now have six tents and three of those are Coleman Tents of various sizes. I have been generally pleased with the products overall, but I do not subject them to harsher environments as I would my Marmot or Eureka.

Warranty - Coleman stepped up and replaced this tent way past the warranty period. We got a rip in one of the sleeves for the main pole. Even though it still sets up OK, we felt it best not to use the tent in case a storm with gusty wing came up (because of the tear).

Hope this helps somebody.

I did not get this for camping, which is the main use for this product. When I go camping I use plastic dinnerware which has worked fine for me.

Why does this “cutlery” set lack a knife? That is a significant omission for a "cutlery" set. $30 is too much to pay for a thin fork and spoon. These are lighter weight than flatware you would use at home, but they are about the same weight as all the other utensils designed for travel or camping. Titanium costs more because it is a rare metal, not because it is superior. If you are traveling by plane and security decides to confiscate your fork, you will be out $15.

For a $30 set that advertises that it is strong, I would expect to get a spoon that is capable of scooping premium ice cream without bending. I just reviewed a stainless-steel spoon that was of higher quality, was much stronger, and cost $3. I mainly use these for typical vacation and work travel, not multi-day hiking and camping, so weight does not matter much. If you are camping then this set is fine, but so is plastic.

Danielson unisex-adult Anchor Pulley Gray One Size I installed one of these on each end of an Old Town Pack canoe.

For installation, I cut a small board to act as platform for the pulley that I mounted onto the canoe. Then attached the pulley onto the board. This was necessary so the pulley would hang out over the end of the canoe enough.

The installation was easy enough with the screws received with the pulleys. But, I purchased separately 1/4" brass screws with nuts as I don't think the small screws would hold for long term. Not really a criticism.

But, the pulley has a restraining device that works very well, if your anchor rope is at least 1/2" diameter. Smaller cord I am using (purchased from Amazon with a Yak Gear Nylon Rope) will not restrain when you release the cord trying to hold the anchor in place. Must instead use cleats to hold the rope, which is difficult when you pull up the anchor and it is dangling off the end of the canoe. I have a 5# mushroom anchor on either end and that is significant weight to tie off.

Not sure this is the final solution with these pulleys and the nylon rope and I may have to go back to using larger diameter rope. Really did not want to do this as this would put more rope cluttering up the canoe when I fish.

These are well made metal anchors. Just not sure about for canoe/yak applications unless you can deal with the additional mass of rope in the boat.

text_fidelity_a:
CamelBak eddy Insulated Water Bottle, 20oz I simply LOVE my insulated Eddy Cambelbak bottle!
I didn't have a clue what they were all about, nor how a bite valve worked, but I needed a water bottle and started reading up about them. I am converted!
This bottle is very well constructed, and although tall, it doesn't take up much space on a desk or side table, and it holds a good 0.6L volume of lovely iced water.....and it doesn't "sweat"! Fantastic!
It keeps my water nice and cool for ages, and it is so convenient that I find myself drinking a lot more water that before, which is a good thing.

For anyone else that doesn't know what bite valve is (can I be the only one??!) - the "spout" of this bottle is made of a firm silicon rubber and it has a closed hole that attaches down to the bottle's straw. When you bite the end of this spout or valve, it squeezes the hole open and you just suck up the water like drinking from a straw. The second you take pressure off and stop biting down, the hole closes shut again and - voila! - A leak proof bottle! It is a fantastic design - I love it! (see pic)

The valve part can be in an angled or upright position, so you don't have to tip the bottle sideways to get the water to flow, and it also pushes right back to a "closed" and flat position which is great if you have it in a backpack, beach bag etc. It is just a really innovative design and it really works so well!!
I highly recommend this bottle to anyone who wants a fantastic, no sweat, leak-proof, easy to use drinking bottle - 10/10 !
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak eddy Insulated Water Bottle, 20oz

text_fidelity_a:
Electric Foot Warmer for Men and Women with Non-Slip，Fast Heating Pad with Four Layer Temperature Locking System,Foot Warmer Under Desk.Electric Foot Heating pad with 3 Temperature Settings. The foot warmer seems to be made of good quality fabric and leather.

The foot warmer has three temperature settings: 38C (100F), 42C (108F), and 55C (131F). When I turned the foot warmer on at room temperature, it listed 22C. I adjusted the temperature to the hottest setting of 55C. I kept it going for 45 minutes, with both my feet in the warmer. After 20 minutes or so the warmer stabilized at a temperature of 43 to 44C. 25 minutes later, the temperature had not changed, never reaching anywhere close to 55C. 44C was warm enough, but not what was promised.

Besides the temperature limit, two drawbacks for me (may not apply to other people):
- The foot warmer has USB-C input, and it comes with a USB-A to USB-C cable. Note that the warmer only accepts 10W, and if you try to use a USB-C to USB-C cable that delivers higher wattage, the foot warmer will not work. Ideally the foot warmer's electronics would be designed to take as much wattage as they need, and no more, in the same way I can connect an iphone and an ipad pro to the same fast-charging brick, and each device would accept only as much wattage as appropriate, instead of burning out or shutting down.

text_fidelity_a: Eagle Claw 04300-005 Invincible Chain Stringer, 46-Inch, 9-Snap,Multi-Color This style of stringer is really the best kind to use if you want to keep your fish alive and well while you are fishing. The nylon versions pile the fish on top of each other, and it literally suffocates them and you end up with a lot of dead fish to clean. (if anyone reading this knows anything about fishing and actually eats the fish they catch like I do....they know that this is kind of a bad thing. makes the meat taste all funky) with this stringer, you can easily pierce the lower lip of the fish (do NOT put it through their gills as this will kill them quicker than anything! just a little tip for those who may not have known this) it will keep them alive pretty much until the time you clean them depending on where and how you transport them to the cleaning station. But essentially it's a good all around stringer that will serve you well if used properly. they DO tend to rust if you let the water dry on them over time especially if used in salt water conditions, but they are pretty inexpensive over all so easy to replace as needed. I will often use this in unison with the nylon stringers to kind of extend the stringer a bit for when I am fishing from the shore as it gives the fish more room to swim around and stay active. but it is a good one for clipping to the side of the kayak or canoe. just don't use it on a motor boat. (Get a livewell or a cooler for that, because speeding through the water on a stringer will actually drowned the fish believe it or not.....yes you can drowned a fish. lol) anyway, hope this helps any beginner anglers out there.
text_fidelity_b: Eagle Claw 04300-005 Invincible Chain Stringer, 46-Inch, 9-Snap,Multi-Color

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Aquaticz Bocce Set I've been trying to up my backyard/pool gaming cred, and these little sacks of fun were next on my list. I've played bocce before, but it's been ages. Much like riding a bike, I was able to remaster the game pretty quick. As a game on grass, this set is a bit lacking. Most bocce balls are waterproof enough and well I don't tend to just leave them in the rain (quite a surprise if you forget them before mowing the lawn!). In the pool these take on a new life. They float! The game is fun in the water but it lacks a certain precision as well things tend to well float away. I'm sure any meaningful competition would need the water jets disabled, but for something to pass the time, they're fun. Oddly enough my [[ASIN:B01BEU86RS Franklin Sports Aquaticz 1 Hole Ball Toss]] game came with solid balls and this these sacks. Much like the end of Ghostbusters (oops spoiler), I crossed the streams. Spoiler alert--it worked! These worked better at corn hole than the solid balls, and the solid balls (that also float) worked better at bocce!

In the end I'm rather happy, but given that I ended up mixing a couple sets up to get that way, I can't say this is a 5 star set. Solid idea, good construction, and all around good idea, but not quite there.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Aquaticz Bocce Set

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon COOLSHOT 40 Golf Laser Rangefinder Works great and is 2/3 or less the price of a comparable Bushnell range finder. I give this 4 instead of 5 stars only because the optics are somewhat sensitive and require the unit to be precisely in front of your pupil to be able to see well. More expensive optics have a slightly more forgiving area in which the image is easily viewed.

More generally, the unit finds targets quickly and appears to generate the same distances as more expensive Bushnell finders. The Nikon may be very slightly slower than the Bushnell at locating a flag stick instead of trees behind it, but I'm talking about 2 seconds instead of 1 second... hardly enough to delay your golf round. The comparable Bushnell range finders are technically better, but can be close to double the price. This Nikon works extremely well. Potentially the biggest problem with the Nikon relative to Bushnell range finders is they are less common. You will have a more difficult time finding accessories like carrying cases and friends who borrow your range finder to shoot a distance are more likely to have to ask you questions about how it works. If you want the absolute best and finest that all your friends can use and that has a bigger selection of third party accessories, get the Bushnell. If you want to save $200 and get a very high performing range finder for yourself, this Nikon is perfect.
text_fidelity_b: Nikon COOLSHOT 40 Golf Laser Rangefinder

text_fidelity_a:
Shoreline Marine Safety Whistle Nice and loud, durable, and it won't rust. This is a decent-quality whistle that I use with my hunting partners so we can keep in contact without scaring away game. They have helped us find each other in the woods, and we sometimes use them just to help us keep track of where each other is, while still hunting. I've also used them to get a bear's attention several times, when I wanted them to see me along salmon streams in Alaska. That usually is enough to encourage the bears to move off and let me pass.

I also keep one on my boat, as a signaling device. Electric horns on boats are notorious for corroding and failing, and the Coast Guard considers these whistles as adequate, which has helped me pass boarding inspections a couple of times. For me, its just cheap insurance that I'll be able to get someone's attention if I need to, or to avoid a ticket in case the Coast Guard wants to do an inspection. I like plastic better than metal for a whistle because its usually more comfortable to use if its cold out.

Let me know if my review was helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Shoreline Marine Safety Whistle

text_fidelity_a:
Harbinger Lifting Grips, Black, Large/X-Large My brother-in-law runs an elite gym primarily for military men/women who need to hone their skills - though their customer base is wide range from children to adult. The whole idea is to push your body to the limits (keeping safety in mind) to achieve your best results in everything from martial arts to boxing to weight training and exercise. He personally used the lifting grips primarily for hanging exercises and stated that he was able to hold on past the point that his hands would have given out. He also used them for weight training and felt he was more in control. He was able to get a longer workout and reach his fitness goals more easily with the help of the grips. His views were echoed by the other clients who tried them (weight of clients ranged from 115lbs to 260lbs). The lifting grips fit with a velcro that goes around your wrist. The thickly padded curve rests against your hand and over the bar. The grips were tried against using regular chalk and lifting gloves. The lifting grips provided better hand protection - preventing callouses and raw hands. Further they provided a longer and stronger lift time than using regular chalk or comparable lifting gloves. It also doesn't have the mess and clean-up that using chalk creates. They are definitely built to last and have been subjected to multiple handling by various trainers and trainees of different sizes/weights. The Large/Xlarge size was perfect for most of the users. Those with smaller hands could still use them but likely would have benefited more with a smaller size. The gym and its patrons will be ordering more of the Harbinger Lifting Grips because of the rave reviews it received from those who used them. Cost wise, $29.99 with free PRIME shipping is a good deal on grips that will last. The price is comparable to retail stores but with free Prime shipping, Amazon was the better deal.
Reviewer note: Because of unexpected hand surgery, I was unable to use the grips and thus required the input from another source. Since my BIL is a certified fitness expert and owns a gym, he was the best choice. To get a better view of the product, clients and staff were asked to try the lifting grips during their workouts.

text_fidelity_a: RaceWax Ski P-tex Base Repair Kit: 10 ptex, Metal Scraper, 3 3M Buffing Pads Got this to do some repair work on my 30 something year old xc skis.  Worked great and so easy to do.  I had some pretty bad gouges and scraps from skiing on frozen gravel.  Spent a bit of time preping the bases by removing the wax base and cleaning up the edges of the gouges.  I also used my waxing iron to preheat the bases.  Lit the candle and moved slowly and carefully.  Keep the candle close to your work and hold it at an angle to keep the carbon to a minimum.  After cooling down the included scraper mad quick work of leveling out the area.  A couple quick passes with the scotch brite pads and a finally buff with the white pad and I was ready for a base wax.  I have only been out once since the repair (figures all the snow melted) but the repair held perfectly.  I used about a third of a candle to repair about 4 ft. of scratches of at least a fingernail width wide.  So much cheaper than a new pair of skis.

text_fidelity_a: Rocket stove with handle, A portable wood burning camping stove with a fire poker & tongs. wood burning Rocket stove with Large Fuel Chamber Best for outdoor cooking. tent heater & emergency. I have messed around with DIY rocket stoves with some success - my best was in using concrete blocks.  They work, but who wants to carry around 4 or 6 concrete blocks in their car?  It's not awful, but this rocket stove is lighter weight and works pretty much the same way.  One really good deal with this rocket stove is that it has the slide on grate pieces so that a pot/pan can be put on top to cook food, boil water for coffee or whatever.  It also gives off heat so when you are out camping, you can sit near it while cooking and not worry about the wind changing direction and open flames burning you as might happen with a regular fire.  Not just that, but with this rocket stove, you can gather small twigs that wouldn't keep a regular fire going and in a rocket stove, they burn well.  I think if I were to make any changes to this design, I'd change the legs.  I'm no engineer, but I think a folding mechanism could be used so the legs are permanently attached, but fold down so the rocket stove is as small as it is now (without the legs being removed and possibly lost).  The same with the slide on grate pieces.  Again, I am not an engineer so it may be that hinges that close to heat might be an issue, but if the grate pieces could be slightly curved so they rest against the stove pipe section, then the same would be accomplished with them as the legs.  The less you have to keep track of, the less that can be lost, right?  Of course if you have a "rocket rucksack" to store it in and maybe the inside is that heat mat stuff so you could place it under the stove while using it and then fold it up to store the stove in it...hey, just some suggestions to the manufacturer for the next iteration!  As far as this rocket stove goes, I am very pleased with it's performance.
text_fidelity_b: Rocket stove with handle, A portable wood burning camping stove with a fire poker & tongs. wood burning Rocket stove with Large Fuel Chamber Best for outdoor cooking. tent heater & emergency.

text_fidelity_a:
Freeze Dried Sliced Strawberries by Nutristore | Pack of 2 | Healthy Snack | Emergency Survival Bulk Food Storage | Amazing Taste & Quality | 25 Year Shelf Life These strawberries are beyond delicious! These big #10 (one gallon) cans of freeze dried fruit are IDEAL if you are new to using freeze dried fruits or if you want to put away a couple cans for your family in case of emergency but you don't want to spend $150 on a 6 can case plus shipping from somewhere else. (You simply cannot beat Amazon Prime!)

• • • #10 cans typically hold 12 cups of food and about 11 cups of freeze dried fruits and veggies • • •

It is hard to find information about how much food is actually in a #10 can and have it be accurate enough that you can plan your meals. When filled to the brim with something like rice, the #10 cans hold 12 cups. But freeze dried food is light and not compacted, with air space between the dry pieces so you get about 11 cups (bananas) to 11.25 cups (strawberries and raspberries) in a big can like this. The cans are "full", the difference is simply air space between the fruit pieces. (To be safe, always assume there are 11 cups per #10 can of freeze dried fruits and veggies. I have found this to be accurate and a great way to calculate how much you have stored.)

Now let's talk about how yummy the food is! As I took pictures I could hardly stop my 9 year old son from grabbing handfuls of strawberries behind my back as I tried to snap a quick photo. (The bowl of strawberries was dumped straight into his mouth mere seconds after I got that picture!) The fruit is positively DELICIOUS for snacking straight from the can!

We live in Houston and personally lived through Hurricane Ike in 2008. At the time my son was 18 months old and I would have given anything - ANYTHING - to have these freeze dried strawberries to have offered him. Grocery stores were picked clean the day before the storm. Some of the grocery stores flooded and most of them had damage to roofs, glass doors and building structures from being hit by flung tree branches, fence pieces and debris. We went 12 days without electricity in our home. Grocery stores were without power for the first 5 or 6 days and stayed closed for about a week in our area as they had to be cleaned up before reopening. It was almost 3 weeks after the storm before stores were restocked with fresh produce beyond a few local items like tomatoes and jalapeños. Please, take the advice from someone who has lived through a natural disaster and invest in freeze dried fruits and veggies for your family. Everything in our refrigerators and freezers were ruined by day 2 without power and we still had 10 days to go. The only thing you have to rely on is what you have on your pantry shelves. That is it. These cans will keep for 25 years unopened and truly are a wise investment.

So, since I have been through a natural disaster, I have learned how to bake with freeze dried food since I still live in Houston and may have to deal with another storm in the future. These strawberries did GREAT and I'm going to include the recipe I used so you can have success with them, too. It is wise to open and try the food you are storing but since this company gave several reviewers like myself a discount to test their products, this work has been done for you. You can simply store the cans of food knowing it is superior quality. (I have purchased and used Thrive brand fruits and these taste identical to theirs! In my opinion these strawberries were even better quality.)

• Strawberry Chocolate Chip Muffins •
--> This recipe also works with freeze dried blueberries or other freeze dried fruits
1/4 cup butter, softened
1/3 cup sugar
1 egg, beaten
1/2 cup milk (a small can of evaporated milk is fine to use)
1 cup flour (up to 1.5 cups depending on humidity; batter should be a thick muffin batter)
1 and 1/2 tsp baking powder
1/2 cup freeze dried strawberries (or raspberries or other fruit) rehydrated in 1/2 cup water with the excess liquid drained off
1/2 cup milk chocolate chips

Preheat oven to 400°. Cream butter and sugar. Add the egg and mix well. Add flour alternately with splashes of milk and combine until a thick batter has formed and all ingredients are incorporated. Gently fold in rehydrated fruit. Spoon into 12 paper lined baking cups, filling halfway to 3/4ths full. Bake for 20 minutes or until tops begin to turn golden.

• Tip •
The leftover powder at the bottom of each can is AWESOME for making strawberry butter or adding to oatmeal to make your own fruit and cream flavor. If nothing else, dump the powder in your pancake batter. Don't let the powder go to waste, it is delicious!

Also, if you want to know about the countries of origin on the fruits, this was posted on the seller's FAQ page: "We source our Nutristore foods from some of the following countries: USA, Canada, Ecuador, Greece, Costa Rica, Uruguay, Argentina, Serbia, New Zealand, India, Poland, Mexico & Chile. [We] no longer source foods from China."

I was very fortunate to be able to purchase this pack of freeze dried strawberries at a discount so I could try it, eat it and bake with it before writing a review. I hope that by sharing my photos and experience that you are able to make the best buying decision for your own family! Hugs from Houston!
text_fidelity_b: Freeze Dried Sliced Strawberries by Nutristore | Pack of 2 | Healthy Snack | Emergency Survival Bulk Food Storage | Amazing Taste & Quality | 25 Year Shelf Life

text_fidelity_a:
Fox Outdoor Products Mission Ready Drop Leg Holster I wanted to try a drop leg holster for some time and came across this model in desert camo through another vendor. For the price, and because I had heard good things about Fox, I decided to take advantage of the reduced price and see how good (or bad) this holster really is.

The first day, after strapping it on and making all the adjustments I could, I carried around a mini ball peen hammer just to try to get used to it. Why did I choose a hammer? While I am CCW licensed, Florida does not currently allow "open carry". So I had to put something of measurable weight in the holster without alarming the neighbors or anyone driving by on our street. I could imagine someone seeing me with a drop leg holster and calling our local law enforcement, not knowing that their was no gun in the holster -- but assuming there was.Yes, the weight of the hammer head made the holster cant backwards, so I switched to a rubber mallet. This provided a much better balance.

Then I switched to a Glock 23 and a Springfield XD-45 MOD 2 and alternately carried both around inside our home, After trying my darndest to get it to fit properly, I came to the following conclusions:

1. This is a cool looking and well constructed rig. The desert camo design is well done, the material is light and flexible, and the various
clips, belts and fasteners work like they should.
2 The holster accommodated both the Springfield and Glock perfectly and the strap easily fastened over the gun butt.
3. It is very light and designed to fit comfortably against your thigh.
4. And of course it easily carries a lighter weight weapon like a Kahr PM9 and a Glock 42. In fact the smaller and lighter pistols eliminate
the bounding around explained below. But who wants to carry a "pocket pistol" in a drop leg holster?

But, and this is a "big but" for me, the single strap that fastens the holster around your thigh just couldn't keep the holster secure and steady. It bounced while walking and really moved around when running (even at my slow pace). I tightened the thigh strap so that over 14" of strap was outside the buckle, but it just never felt secure. No one wants that feeling -- you want your gun to be right where it's supposed to be -- all of the time.

This holster really needs two improvements: 1. It needs a second strap to go around the thigh, one high and one low. 2. It also needs more vertical adjustment so that it can be carried a bit higher on your belt. Both of these changes would result in a better fit and should eliminate excess movement.
text_fidelity_b: Fox Outdoor Products Mission Ready Drop Leg Holster

There is supposedly a way to do it, laying it on the ground and pulling it... we have not tried it. In our methods (*** the frame) we slightly twisted it. It still stands fine, but because we tried this other way... anyways, I’ve not wanted to get back into this so we haven’t tried yet. Worse case, it gets laid out in the back of our Prius. We hope this new method helps. But I’m too weary to try - yet. We will, eventually.

While this is very frustrating and I have considered giving it a 4 star rating because of it, I still like the rest of the set up and I think it’ll help, that I decided to still give it the 5 stars. BUT... do yourself a favor and find those videos and preplan.

NcStar 1" High Ring with Weaver (RB13) I used these to mount a 50mm whitetail scope on a .308 FAL. The clearance is not enough to also use the peep sight, but that's because the scope is 50mm -- a 40mm scope would have allowed me to still use the peeps.

We've put about 100 rounds downrange on two different outings after zeroing and the scope has held zero fine, so I know the rings aren't moving despite the .308 recoil.

Some people think these rings aren't solid enough but I feel they are great. Just make sure you tighten the hex screws and the mounting nuts tightly, AND make sure your rail mount is also tight. Check the fasteners periodically if you're using a high-recoil rifle.

Only complaint I have is that the hex screw sockets (the part the hex wrench fits into) aren't sturdy enough to really hold up to a lot of cranking. I noticed one of the screw sockets started rounding out and it became more and more difficult to screw or unscrew with the included wrench. If I ever have to take this scope off, I won't be surprised if have to replace one or more hex screws.

Still, a good quality product for the price and I give it 5 stars.

text_fidelity_a:
Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire I purchased Campy Shamal 2-way rims a couple years back. I then purchased everything needed to mount and maintain tubeless tires including Fusion 3s. I ride a '12 Specialized S-Works Roubaix and mostly do fast training rides about 3 to 4 days a week with longer rides beyond 60 miles fairly regularly. I weigh out at roughly 185 pounds.

Tubeless and ceramic bearings are somewhat in the same category these days in terms of bikers wondering if this equipment truly makes a difference. Well, I've ridden ceramic bearings in my crank and in my wheels...and YES...it makes a difference...now...I've ridden on tubeless for two riding seasons...and YES...they make a difference. Tubeless is the future...as it is in nearly every vehicle that has wheels from a riding mower to a motorcycle to a car...and mountain bikes. Why it has taken so long with road biking is understandable...change is hard...and manufacturers will go where the money is.

First, let me make this clear...putting the Fusion 3 tires on was a chore...and I mean...a CHORE. It will test your patience. Do NOT succumb to using levers as it will ruin the bead. Google tubeless tire installation for help but even then it will baffle you as to how you're going to get that tire over the rim...but...you will...and the benefits will be worth it.

Second, it takes a few rides to get the tires truly seated. Use an air compressed pump if you've got it...but...I had a "Joe Blow" floor pump that worked fine. I didn't install the sealant until after the second short ride and pump up. You will most likely lose quite a bit of air at first but as the tire seals over time...the air pressure stabilized. I do pump up my tires before every ride but it isn't out of the norm of my former clincher tires.

Third, I've ridden my fusion 3s at 90psi on the front tire and 100psi on the back. The ride is fast & super smooth. A lot of riders think super high psi is better but that is, (arguably for some), not true because at a high psi your tire is actually bumping up and down off the road which drains energy transfer over time. The benefit of running tubeless at lower psi is that the tire remains in more constant contact with the road which...over time...equals better energy transfer...and hence...speed, comfort, and endurance. Also, there is some evidence that without a tube you eliminate friction...I'm honestly not sure about that claim...even so, I can say from experience that I'm not going back to tubed tires...tubeless tires run as advertised.

Fourth, durability...I run typical roads here in Maryland over countless miles...up and down hills...less maintained side roads...and these Fusion 3s can go yet another season. The wear is normal with no unusual issues. I've NOT had one flat tire. I've NOT added more sealant since the first install...which I should've done...but...it hasn't made a difference.

Fifth, the only reservation I have is getting a flat tire but I guess it's a good thing that I'm not as use to dealing with flats like I had for my tubed tires. I have to say it has been a pleasure to not have had one flat for two seasons.

I'd like to try the ATOM version of this tire...and I think I'll get it just for comparison purposes. Not looking forward to the install and my expectation is that they will not fit my riding style, endurance expectations, and my higher weight...even so, I'm a believer in trying anything once...so...we'll see.

All in all...educate yourself but don't be afraid to go tubeless. It is change that we all seem to avoid but I'll never go back now that I've tried it out...and as the biking money goes...tubeless quality and selection will as well. ENJOY!
text_fidelity_b: Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire

Titan Fitness HD Multi-Grip Wall Mounted Pull-Up Bar, 48" Wide Grip, Rated 600 LB, Strength Accessory I'll come back to post pics. yes hardware to install would be nice, but people install to diff. surfaces and would need diff. hardware.

I used 2 2x6 boards to mount to studs. I would recommend using 2x8 if I did it again. I anchored them with 8 - 5" lag bolts at the outer edges and 12 - 4" structural screws at the middle studs.

for anyone having problems getting the lags in that are on the upper side of the bottom bracket. mount the top section of the pull bar first. drill your pilot holes in the correct location for the bottom brackets. once you've done this, hand thread in your lag bolt with the bracket free. tighten the bolt down almost all the way then reattach the top of the pull up bar to the support bracket with the supplied bolts. you might have to flex the upper section to align the bolt holes. if you don't do this you'll have to angle the lag bolts in.

I had both my 2 sons on this and myself and it's holding strong. roughly 300lbs. My wife has said the bar is smaller diameter than our current pull up bar. I don't think it'll be an issue. I do like the fact that I can finally do wide pull ups again. Being able to reach out the entire width of the bar is nice. I also like the different angles on the hand holds.

text_fidelity_a:
Igloo Thermoelectric Iceless 28-40 Qt Electric Plug-in 12V Coolers This served me well for three weeks on the road. The items you put in this need to start out cold and you need to buy a separate wall adapter for hotel rooms. I bought a cheap one from Coolbuy that worked well. This cooler does seem to keep the temperature cool when left in the car overnight though. This is easy to clean because the motor is on the top.

One issue I had is that after a couple weeks I noticed standing water on the bottom which soaked some items I had. I am not sure if that was from condensation or if a bottle leaked a bit. It would be good if this came with a small removable platform to keep items off the very bottom in case condensation starts to puddle.

The lid is heavy and can pinch your hand if it slams shut.

The cord placement is not ideal because it blocks some of the handle movement when plugged in. This is an issue because the handle needs to be in a certain position for the top to open fully.

Update. I have used this on more trips and have concluded that the condensation is from the cooler. The cooling fins ice over and then melt when the temperature rises high enough. I routinely see pools of water on the right side that soak anything underneath. This cooler is a damp cool, not a dry cool like a regular freezer. This is problematic for anything made of paper or cardboard in the cooler. I am lowering my rating to three stars.

My fix was to use plastic risers that came with some stay-fresh plastic containers meant to hold vegetables. It adds about one centimeter of space between the cooler contents and the bottom where the water pools.
text_fidelity_b: Igloo Thermoelectric Iceless 28-40 Qt Electric Plug-in 12V Coolers

For the price, I would like to see better engineering. While I understand this is an entry level pulse monitor, set-up is an unnecessary challenge.

Schrade Bedrock TiNi with 1095 High Carbon Steel Blade for Buschcrafting I’m a very satisfied buyer who has only just opened the box. I’m not a knife expert, just someone who wanted a good, inexpensive survival type knife.

My knife was delivered razor sharp and as flawless as a $37 knife can be – perhaps as flawless as knives costing substantially more. I read many reviews of this knife prior to purchase and agree that it falls comfortably into the category of survival knife rather than fighting knife.

A couple suggestions. First, check the tightness of all four handle screws with a 2.5mm hex/Allen wrench before you use the knife for anything as they all needed tightening on mine. You might also consider using red thread locker to further secure them. The combination of these two adjustments should eliminate any problem of the grips loosening. To me, the large grips feel just great and I have medium sized hands. Second, the sheath is amazingly adequate. If you feel the sheath rides too low, take it to a sewing or shoe repair shop and either have them move the inner piece of Velcro lower on the sheath or sew an additional piece below the existing piece, which will allow you to fold the outside flap down further thus raising the sheath on your belt. I like the adjustable length handle strap w/snap and detachable front pouch on the sheath.

No doubt this a hefty blade. It may not win any beauty contests or look as threatening as a combat knife, but it looks fully functional for the purpose for which it was intended. I look forward to many years of satisfied service from it.
text_fidelity_b: Schrade Bedrock TiNi with 1095 High Carbon Steel Blade for Buschcrafting

text_fidelity_a:
WATERH Smart Water Bottle - Tracks Hydration Intake, Analyzes TDS Water Quality, LED Glow Reminder via Bluetooth. Hack Your Hydration Health, 18 oz The WATERH bottle looks and feels solid. It's comfortable to grab for a person with large hands like me, but I wonder how a person with smaller hands would feel about it. I have certainly used other "non-smart" bottles that feel better in my hands. The cap is functional, though I would have preferred a type of cap that has a spout or similar mechanism. For example, I love the Zojirushi cap that (1) keeps any parts where you place your lips clean (WATERH does that), (2) can be operated with one hand (WATERH does NOT do that; you need a hand to hold the bottle and the second one to open the cap), and (3) is easy to clean (the WATERH cap has some tight spaces that are hard to clean).

The bottle has a water sensor inside, as well as some kind of scales at the bottom of the bottle that helps the app determine how much water you have consumed. The bottle needs to be charged by resting it on a USB-C base charger, included with the product. I've been using the water bottle for a couple of days, and the bottle battery is at 97%, so apparently it will last quite long.

The bottle has a led ring near the base that reminds you when to drink. The led light is also used to display when the bottle is charging, when it is fully charged, etc.

The application is pretty basic and bare bones. The Apple Store display pretty bad customer reviews. I haven't found it to be bad. The only missing feature that is important to me is an automatic connection with Apple's Health application. Adding that feature would make much more useful to me.

The manufacturer states that "WaterH is equipped with a built-in TDS (Total Dissolved Solids) sensor meter so you can know exactly what's in your bottle. Stop guessing the quality of your water through taste or smell." The sensor is likely there, but I have found not way to access those results. There are no instructions, and exploring the app yielded nothing.

Bottomline: the WATERH water bottle is a fun gimmick, but not really necessary. Regardless of how you do it, drink plenty of water.
text_fidelity_b: WATERH Smart Water Bottle - Tracks Hydration Intake, Analyzes TDS Water Quality, LED Glow Reminder via Bluetooth. Hack Your Hydration Health, 18 oz
